name: chemprob

relevance.justification: Directly aligned with BioThings entity types. Contains 603 chemoproteomic probes (chemical compounds with InChIKey), 1,016 competitors (small molecules with InChIKey/SMILES), and 14,250 human protein targets (UniProt IDs). Probe-protein covalent interaction data maps directly to MyChem.info (chemicals) and links to MyGene targets. Structured tabular data, actively updated (last updated Sep 2024).

novelty.justification: First atlas of chemoproteomic probes (CPPs) labelling human proteins in living cells. Unique data: 603 CPPs (133 covalent ABPP + 470 photoaffinity PAL-AfBPP), 1,016 competitors, 135,486 probe-labelled binding sites across 13 amino acid residue types in 13,938 proteins, 2,118,636 binding ratio records. This data type — probe-protein covalent labeling in living cells — is not in any BioThings API. CysDB (predecessor) only covers cysteine-binding probes; Chem(Pro)2 covers all 13 amino acid types. ChEMBL/BindingDB lack this probe-specific covalent interaction paradigm.

openness.justification: Freely accessible at chemprosquare.idrblab.net without login. Download files are publicly accessible via direct URLs (text/plain, no auth required). No explicit license statement found on site, but paper states 'open to all users without any login requirement'. From idrblab (same group as TTD/PDCdb which use CC BY-NC 4.0). Assuming CC BY-NC 4.0 pending license confirmation — compatible with BioThings academic/non-commercial use.

evidence.scope: Chemoproteomic probes (CPPs) — covalent and photoaffinity probes that label human proteins in living cells. Covers probe structures (SMILES, InChIKey), competitor compounds, probe-protein covalent interactions, binding sites (amino acid residue level), quantitative binding ratios, and cell systems used. 603 probes, 1,016 competitors, 14,250 protein targets, 2,118,636 binding ratio records.
evidence.overlap: Minimal overlap with existing BioThings sources. ChEMBL/BindingDB cover non-covalent ligand-protein interactions but not probe-specific covalent labeling. CovalentInDB and CysDB cover a small subset (cysteine only). The full CPP atlas (all amino acids, photoaffinity probes, living cell validation) is entirely novel.

license.name: CC BY-NC 4.0 (assumed, consistent with other idrblab databases)
restrictions: Non-commercial use only — BioThings academic deployment compatible

risks: License not explicitly stated on site — assumed CC BY-NC 4.0 based on other idrblab databases; should confirm
